title: Samsung Eyes Massive NAND Production Upgrade in China as AI Storage Demand Soars!
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Samsung Electronics is reportedly accelerating its semiconductor manufacturing upgrades in China, aiming to increase ninth-generation vertical NAND (V9) production fivefold at its Xi’an X2 fabrication facility by late 2027.

The South Korean technology giant's strategy comes amid rapidly growing demand for enterprise storage solutions driven by artificial intelligence infrastructure expansion.
Samsung Targets 50,000 Wafers per Month​According to Seoul Economic Daily, Samsung plans to increase monthly V9 NAND production capacity from approximately 10,000 to 50,000 300mm silicon wafers at its Xi’an X2 facility.

The company reportedly intends to convert 20–30% of its existing sixth-generation V-NAND production lines to V9 technology while installing additional equipment in unused cleanroom space.

Equipment installation is expected to begin in February 2027, with production line upgrades targeted for completion by November 2027.
AI Infrastructure Drives NAND Demand​Samsung’s ninth-generation V-NAND technology features 286 layers, enabling greater storage density and supporting high-capacity enterprise solid-state drives (eSSDs).

These storage products play an increasingly important role in AI data centers, where large-scale computing workloads require efficient access to vast quantities of information.

The transition toward advanced NAND manufacturing could help Samsung capitalize on growing enterprise storage demand while improving its product mix.
Competition Intensifies in China​The reported upgrades also come as Chinese semiconductor manufacturer Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC) strengthens its competitive position in the global NAND market.

Meanwhile, South Korean rival SK Hynix is pursuing similar technological upgrades at its Dalian manufacturing facility.

Samsung previously told Reuters that its modernization efforts comply with U.S. export regulations and do not involve increasing overall manufacturing capacity or constructing new factories.

By transitioning existing production infrastructure toward more advanced memory technology, Samsung could strengthen its competitiveness, improve manufacturing efficiency and capture greater opportunities in the expanding AI storage market.

The initiative underscores the growing strategic importance of NAND flash memory alongside high-bandwidth memory in the global artificial intelligence supply chain.
